title: What's your money personality?
intro: Six quick questions, about a minute. You'll get your money personality and the three moves that will help you most right now.

questions.q: When you open your banking app, you usually...

a.avoider: Don't, unless I really have to
a.spender: Check the balance before I buy something
a.juggler: Check which bill or card payment is due next
a.saver: Look at my savings and wonder if it should be doing more

questions.q: Payday arrives. What happens to the money?

a.avoider: Honestly, I'm not sure where it goes
a.spender: A little treat first, then I figure out the rest
a.juggler: Bills and card payments, in whatever order is most urgent
a.saver: Some goes to savings before I spend anything

questions.q: A surprise $400 car repair lands. You...

a.avoider: Put it on a card and try not to think about it
a.spender: Card it, and cut back... probably
a.juggler: Add it to the pile I'm already paying down
a.saver: Pay it from savings. Annoying, but fine

questions.q: Which feeling sounds most like you?

a.avoider: Low-level dread; I'd rather not look
a.spender: Money just... disappears, and I'm not sure where
a.juggler: Stress about debts and due dates
a.saver: I save, but I'm not sure I'm doing enough

questions.q: How many subscriptions are you paying for?

a.avoider: No idea, and that's a little scary
a.spender: Quite a few, and I use most of them
a.juggler: I've cut some to free up money for payments
a.saver: I know exactly, down to the dollar

questions.q: Pick one win for the next six months:

a.spender: Stop running out of money before payday
a.juggler: Pay off a credit card for good

avoider.name: The Avoider
avoider.summary: You're not bad with money; you're busy, and looking at it feels bad, so you don't. That's the most common money personality there is, and the easiest to fix, because the first step is just looking.
moves: Do Day 1 of the free reset: find your real take-home pay and fixed bills (15 minutes).
/free/
Hunt down forgotten subscriptions in 10 minutes.
/blog/find-and-cancel-subscriptions/
Set three bank alerts so your accounts warn you before problems happen.
/free/

spender.name: The Spender
spender.summary: You enjoy your money, which is good. The problem isn't spending; it's that you can't see the limit until it's gone. One weekly spending number fixes that without tracking every coffee.
moves: Set one weekly spending number instead of a dozen categories.
/blog/how-to-make-a-budget-you-will-keep/
Turn 'surprise' costs into sinking funds so they stop wrecking the month.
/blog/sinking-funds-explained/
Audit subscriptions and keep only the ones you'd sign up for again today.
/blog/find-and-cancel-subscriptions/

juggler.name: The Juggler
juggler.summary: You're on top of due dates, but debt is doing the steering. You don't need more willpower; you need a payoff order and an end date you can see.
moves: Pick avalanche or snowball with the real maths, and point every extra dollar at one debt.
/blog/debt-avalanche-vs-snowball/
Check whether a balance transfer would actually save you money.
/compare/best-balance-transfer-cards/
Build a $1,000 starter emergency fund so new surprises stop going on cards.
/blog/how-to-build-an-emergency-fund/

saver.name: The Cautious Saver
saver.summary: You've got the hardest habit down: you save. Now your money could be doing more. The next step is making sure savings earn a real rate and that long-term money is invested, simply and cheaply.
moves: Claim your full 401(k) match if your job offers one.
/blog/401k-match-explained/
Start investing with $100 a month, step by step.
/blog/how-to-start-investing-with-100-a-month/
Make sure your savings sit in an insured, high-yield account.
/compare/best-high-yield-savings-accounts/
